1. General
This document defines the technical requirements and acceptance criteria for needle coke
intended for the production of Ultra High Power (UHP) graphite electrodes and nipples. It
covers the technical specifications of needle coke, qualification requirements for approved
suppliers, qualified laboratories, inspection requirements and sampling procedures to be
applied throughout the procurement process.
2. Standards
In general, the standards applicable to this field are listed in Table 1.
Table 1 – General Standards
Abbreviation Full Name
ISO International Organization for Standardization
ASTM American Society for Testing and Materials
YB/T Ferrous Metallurgy Industry Standard (Recommended)
GB/T National Standard of China (Recommended)
T/ZGTS Association Standard of the Carbon Industry
The standards for the physical and chemical properties of coke are mainly found in ISO, ASTM
and the equivalent Chinese standards (GB/T and YB/T).
These standards also cover the basic parameters for the characterization of coking feedstock (CSO).

3. Technical Specifications of Needle Coke
Table 3 presents the technical specifications for Grade A Needle Coke. The specifications are defined
by acceptable minimum and maximum limits and approved operating ranges.
Values within the Penalty Range are acceptable only with the contractual penalties defined in the
purchase agreement. Any value outside the Penalty Limits shall be deemed unacceptable, and the
entire lot shall be rejected.
Table 3 – Technical Specifications for Grade A Needle Coke
Parameter Unit Value Standard
Moisture m-% max 0.1 GB/T 2001 or ASTM D3173
Volatile Matter m-% max 0.2 YB/T 5189 or ASTM D3175
Ash Content m-% max 0.04 GB/T 1429 or ASTM D4422
Sulfur m-% max 0.4 GB/T 24526 or ASTM D1552
Nitrogen m-% max 0.2 GB/T 19227 or ASTM D5373
Bulk Density t/m3 min 0.92 GB/T 21354 or ISO 1014
Real Density t/m3 min 2.14 GB/T 32158 or ASTM D5004
CTE (30–600 °C) 1/°C max 0.9 × 10⁻⁶ GB/T 37308 or ASTM D6745
Vibrated Bulk Density (1 mm – 2 mm) t/m3 min 0.97 ASTM D4292
Specific Electrical Resistance µΩm 450–550 ISO 10143
Specific Heat (for information) kJ/kg·K approx. 0.99 ASTM E1269
Dedusting Oil m-% max 0.1 ISO 8723
Grain Stability m-% min 90 ASTM D6791

4. Product Sampling
Sampling shall be performed in accordance with ASTM D346 and ASTM D2234. Sampling may be
carried out at different stages of production and logistics, including packaging and pre-shipment inspection.
4.1. Sampling at Supplier Warehouse or Customs Warehouse (Before Shipment)
Sampling shall be carried out at the supplier's warehouse or customs warehouse prior to loading.
Considering the preferred packaging (Big Bags), a total of √N+1 bags shall be randomly selected
from N Big Bags in accordance with the contractual requirements.
From each selected Big Bag, increments shall be collected from four different depths (L/6, L/3,
2L/3 and 5L/6) measured from the top surface of the bag, in the quantities specified by the standards.
The increments collected from each bag shall be thoroughly mixed to form an individual composite sample.
Accordingly, √N+1 composite samples shall be obtained, each of which shall be labelled and sealed.
One quarter of each sealed sample shall be separated with a riffle splitter, packed, labelled with the
same identification code and resealed.
All quartered samples shall then be submitted to the Reference Laboratory for Particle Size Distribution (PSD) analysis.
Corvane Technical Office
Document Title Needle Coke Rev.
Page 6 of 7
Document No. A
Upon receipt and approval of the PSD test results, the remaining portions of the samples shall be
combined and homogenized. The resulting bulk sample shall then be divided into four equal portions
using a riffle splitter.
The four samples shall be identically labelled and sealed and shall be distributed respectively to
the Buyer, Seller, Reference Laboratory and Inspection Company.
The sample allocated to the Reference Laboratory shall be subjected to the tests specified in Table 3,
and the test results shall be reported accordingly.
The inspection stages are presented in Table 4.
The Seller, Inspection Company and Buyer shall each retain their samples for a minimum period of
one (1) year, so that repeat testing can be performed in the event of any dispute.
5. Visual Inspection and Documentation
During inspection (packaging stage and pre-shipment stage), the inspector shall assess:
• Packaging Quality;
• Storage Conditions;
• Presence of Dust Contamination;
• Environmental Cleanliness and Contamination Risks.
The inspector shall also record all stages with photographs, including:
• Inspection Activities;
• Sampling Operations;
• PSD Testing;
• Preparation of Composite Samples.
The Seller should provide written instructions for the long-term storage of the purchased needle coke, including:
• Storage Temperature;
• Relative Humidity Limits;
• Any Additional Preservation Requirements.

Table 4 – Inspection and Test Plan (ITP)
Stage Activity Tests Responsible Parties Status* Acceptance Criteria
Before Packaging Sampling Moisture, Volatile Matter, Ash Content, Sulfur, Nitrogen Manufacturer and Inspection Company Witness
Bulk Density, Real Density, CTE (30–600 °C), Vibrated Bulk Density (1 mm – 2 mm)
Specific Heat, Dedusting Oil, Grain Stability, Strength, PSD
All results shall comply with the requirements specified in Table 3.
Any measured value that exceeds the specified limits after considering the laboratory's
reported measurement uncertainty shall be considered non-conforming.
Before Shipment Sampling and Documentation Review (Section 7) Inspection Company and Reference Laboratory Hold
Moisture, Volatile Matter, Ash Content, Sulfur, Nitrogen, Bulk Density, Real Density
CTE (30–600 °C), Vibrated Bulk Density, Specific Heat, Dedusting Oil, Grain Stability, Strength, PSD
Any measured value outside the limits shall be considered unacceptable.
* Witness (Optional Surveillance): The inspector shall be notified before the activity starts and
may attend the inspection or testing at his discretion. If the inspector fails to attend at the
scheduled time, the manufacturer may proceed with the activity and record the results.
* Hold: The contractor shall notify the inspector before the activity starts. Continuation of the
activity is subject to the inspector's presence and written approval.
